With the Steam summer sale ongoing, what are your favourite Early Access games so far and which should definitely be avoided?
What are your best and worst Early Access experiences so far?

My favourites so far include Broforce, a 2d side-scrolling shooter. I'm really enjoying playing as the latest Bro, Brodator (the Broforce version of Predator). I highly recommend the game.

Also on my recommendation list is Rimworld. It's not on Steam but it's great fun. You build your base on an alien planet and survive against enemy attacks, bad weather, etc. It's really in-depth and just received an update adding traps and improved AI.

I like Prison Architect (200+ hours played) but the simulation isn't as in-depth as I'd like yet and the game slows right down when you have more prisoners than your computer can handle. This is particularly worrying as you're forced to choose between smaller prisons or slower speeds. Mass riots just aren't as much fun with fewer prisoners.

Invisible Inc. is out of Early Access now, but I'm quite disappointed. It's just not as enjoyable as it was last year in Early Access. Even in easy mode, you have to plan every move and think ahead. The older versions just seemed to cut you a bit more slack and weren't as difficult.

I'm not against it being difficult on higher levels, but sometimes you just want to relax and the game just doesn't seem to accommodate that anymore.

Sidechains And Lightning, The New New Bitcoin | TechCrunch

Pretty great breakdown of the groundbreaking stuff coming out of Blockstream. Bitcoin will likely be an entirely different beast in a few years.

On Sidechains:

The sidechains vision of the future is of a vast globe-spanning decentralized network of many blockchains, an intertwined cable rather than a single strand, each with its own protocol, rules, and features — but all of them backed by Bitcoin, and protected by the Bitcoin mining network, as the US dollar was once backed by gold. Sidechains can also be used to prototype changes to the fundamental Bitcoin blockchain. One catch, though: this will require a small tweak to the existing Bitcoin protocol.

On Lightning:

The Lightning Network allows for the creation of “micropayment channels” across which multiple Bitcoin transactions can be securely performed without interacting with the blockchain, except for the initial transaction that initiates the channel. There is no counterparty risk: if any party ceases to cooperate, and/or does not respond within an agreed-on time limit, the channel can be closed and all its outstanding transactions kicked up to the blockchain to be settled there.

The article is easy to digest. Give it a read if you want a glimpse of where we're heading.
